interactions.flavorLineOne: "You killed it! So proud, y'know? Love this whole thing we've got going on, I gotta say—couldn't ask for a more proactive partner. Oh, I got a little something for ya!" —Fynch
"I… I don't know what to say. Usually I'm just, y'know, invisible to folks. But you—you really helped me out of a bind with the Hive. I won't forget that!" —Fynch

"Hey, bud. What brings you back to my little corner of Savathûn's throne world?" Fynch asks as you hand him a Lucent Crunch cookie.

"Is… is this… NO WAY! It's the Dawning already? And you made ME a cookie? I can't believe it… time just flies by when you're in a pocket dimension disconnected from material reality, you know?

"Thank you, Guardian, from the bottom of my, heart—shell—core… that's the one. Seriously, it means a lot that you thought of me like this. My OWN cookie!"

"Tell you what. Bake anymore of these, and I'll wake up the big guy for a treat, assuming he can behave himself. Not when you're around, of course. Maybe he'll have a change of heart after he tastes your baking!"

The rebellious Hive Ghost, Fynch, doesn't believe the Hive deserve the Light, so he offers to work with you to uncover Savathûn's scheme. He provides your first lead: a Hive temple hidden in a dark corner of the Throne World. 

Complete "The Ghosts" mission in the Throne World.
"A curse? Killing Sav's worm? Yeah, okay, I think I can maybe help with that! Take this casing—it's enchanted with all sorts of Hive magics. Could be your solution!" —Fynch

"Ah yes, good stuff, Qualichor. Except not good, actually. Very bad." Fynch nudges a small vial to catch the single, putrid drop your efforts have created. "Made from brain juice and nightmares. Yeah, it's liquid Deepsight, but brew it just right, and it'll 'bring memories into present reality.' That's what the Witches said, at least. Don't think anyone ever tried refining it like this before, though. Anyway, I know this place where the Hive used to store some great artifact. Why don't you head over there, chug this refined Qualichor, and help yourself to the memory of something nice. I'm almost certain you won't go blind!"

Fynch is excited to hear of our progress and lets us in on another lead. 

Hidden in the Throne World is a monument to Savathûn's brother, Oryx. Fynch believes that location might hold more information about how Savathûn acquired the Light.

Complete "The Lightblade" strike in the Throne World.

"I, uh, got just the thing to get power back into that Cryptoglyph—a lead… location! Should aid you in finding some runes to power it back up." —Fynch

Travel to the Temple of the Cunning to locate a Cryptoglyph Rune.

Rhulk, Disciple of the Witness, is dead thanks to the efforts of valiant and determined Guardians.

Without him, the Sunken Pyramid is up for grabs—and the Scorn intend to take control of it on behalf of the Witness.

Take this chance to stop them and keep the Pyramid under Vanguard control in the Preservation activity.

The rebellious Hive Ghost, Fynch, doesn't believe the Hive deserve the Light, so he offers to work with you to uncover Savathûn's scheme. He provides your first lead: a Hive temple hidden in a dark corner of the Throne World. 

Complete "The Ghosts" mission in the Throne World.

"So listen, Savathûn's got this fountain of power nearby. She calls it the Wellspring. Now the Hive and Scorn are fighting over it. Might need to, y'know, get involved…" —Fynch

On the Throne World map, select The Wellspring and complete the activity.

Fynch checks the surroundings, his squirrelly affect shifting into a quieter, tenser mode. He whispers that he has proof of the Lucent Brood's shady schemes. 

He transmats a strange, gleaming fragment in the air before you. As it drops into your open hands, it sends a slight but distinctly paracausal pulse through your palms. 

Fynch explains that he swiped it from the apothecary wing in Savathûn's fortress. He isn't exactly sure what it is, but he's convinced that it's meant to play an important part in some twisted ritual. 

Bring the fragment to the Hidden in the Enclave for analysis.

"Longer I'm here, the more the brood'll start wondering where my Knight and I are at. But hey, if you deal with the Scorn for me, I can go claim the credit! So, uh, good luck?" —Fynch

Keep Fynch's cover by helping him help you.

"I used to get real lonely here, but you? You keep showing up for me again and again. So lemme give back a bit, yeah? I happened to locate a couple of Savathûn's loyalists. Have fun!" —Fynch

Follow Fynch's guidance and hunt down some elite members of Savathûn's guard.

Variks is alarmed to hear about Eramis's lieutenants using Stasis. The situation is more dire than he realized.

He wants to remain on Europa in order to help other Eliksni who wish to flee Eramis, and asks you to help set up a comms network using a nearby array. That way, he can communicate with his allies and prepare for evacuation.

Help Variks set up the patrols network in Charon's Crossing.

Variks disapproves of your new Stasis abilities. He thinks you're being reckless. He warns you to remember what the Darkness has done and what it is doing to Eramis. He refuses to believe that this is the only way to stop her.

But he acknowledges that you are free to walk your own path, even if it's a dangerous one. He urges you not to lose sight of your goal. To get to Eramis, you must begin by defeating the leader of her army: Phylaks. Thanks to his secret communication network, Variks learned that Phylaks was ordered to take control of an area currently occupied by the Vex.

Gather information about the whereabouts of Phylaks, the Warrior by challenging her soldiers in Eventide Ruins.

Variks is surprised and impressed that you managed to defeat Phylaks. He now believes you may be capable of wielding Stasis without being corrupted.

He tells you that your next target is Praksis, the Eliksni who created the technology that allows House Salvation to wield Darkness. Defeat him and Eramis's plans will come to a halt. Variks believes he's been experimenting on the Vex, and if you disrupt his experiments, you might get his attention.

Investigate Praksis, the Technocrat's plans in Asterion Abyss.

Variks looks somber. When he witnessed Eramis releasing the Vex, he realized that she has truly lost sight of what she was fighting for. Now she has endangered everything the Eliksni have built on Europa.

As the Vex make their way across Europa and towards Riis-Reborn, Variks is planning to help some of his allies evacuate the city. They are carrying an important asset that he claims will be invaluable to House Light on Earth. He asks for your help defending them, and then the way will be clear for you to confront Eramis.

Help Variks evacuate the allied Fallen in Eventide Ruins.

Variks tells you about Eramis, a new Kell of the Fallen, or the Eliksni, as they call themselves. Through communing with Pyramids, she has managed to harness the power of Darkness and use it as a weapon.

Variks escaped with proof of that Dark power, asking for help. If Eramis succeeds in giving this power to all of her Eliksni followers, nothing, not even the Guardians, will be able to defeat her.

Variks asks you to find Eramis immediately. Perhaps she can still be stopped.

Pursue Eramis, Kell of Darkness. Complete "The New Kell" mission.

interactions.flavorLineOne: Your clan's reputation grows, and with it your rewards.

Represent your clan well, Guardian.

This banner will grow in strength as your clan demonstrates its power.
For a split second, it seemed like Louis was staring at you. Hawthorne didn't seem to notice. She accepts the gift on his behalf.
Hawthorne is impressed by your dedication to bringing more Guardians into the fold, and she offers a reward in return.

"Love letters? The latest Omolon catalogue? Criminal activity? Whatever it is, you're real popular these days, Guardian."

Hawthorne flips a hawk-nibbled envelope over to you. The letter inside reads,

"To the Hero of the City,

"Curiouser and curiouser! A whole Salvation gang absconding with a Ketch, and a Golden Age AI locked up on a station alone… well, that's news plenty would pay for. A BrayTech AI is a valuable thing, no matter how poor her personal attitude. We'd better make sure she doesn't fall into the wrong hands.

"While you were clearing the nest, I had my people doing some digging on the side. Their key discovery was that many mysteries still wait in Europa's orbit. More investigation means more profit, and an answer to some lingering questions, eh?

"My last contract with a Lightbearer ended… unhappily, let's say. But I believe ours will be a fruitful partnership.

"As ever, your friend, the Spider."

Return to the "Vesper's Host" dungeon and uncover its secrets.

Hawthorne raises her eyebrows at you. "Your correspondent has graduated from letters to packages. I'm telling you, Guardian, you're putting Kadi out of business like this."

You tear open the latest envelope from Spider and a data chip falls out. The attached message reads,

"Dear Guardian,

"We've learned so much together, haven't we? I treat my partners well. Look at how high my last partner has risen in City authority. Always remember what Spider can do for you.

"Now, for Vesper Station… There's an ultimate control mechanism. Bray's personal key. And if you control the AI, you control the station. Vesper Central seems lonely up there. A bit out of control. I think you'll agree she could use a guiding hand.

"My agents have turned up one little key on their search for the big one. You take it and you grab what you want, and you remember it was your old chum who had you in his thoughts this whole time.

"XOXO, etc, the Spider."

PERMISSIONS GRANTED:
TechAccess|Storage|Restricted|42

"A mind heist?" Hawthorne says with a laugh, shaking her head. "Only you, Guardian. Only you."

She turns to look out over the City for a moment, then up to the sky. "I'm glad you helped Eris out, but Ikora found out about everything. You can't keep much from her Hidden. I hear she's authorizing future dives into the Mindscape…"

Hawthorne turns back to you. "Hopefully, Eris got what she was looking for. Because it sounds like you two opened a door that should have stayed closed."

"No one will tell me what happened down there," Hawthorne says with a nervous look back at Ikora. "Whenever I ask, she says it's 'privileged information' and shuts me down."

Anxiously looking around, Hawthorne shakes her head. "I won't ask you to go against Ikora's wishes. She's gotta be keeping secrets for a good reason. But I haven't seen her that shaken since she learned about Savathûn having the Light…"

Hawthorne furrows her brow and stares into the distance for a moment. "Actually… maybe it's better if I don't know, " she murmurs, shifting her attention back to you. "Sometimes the truth is more terrifying than your own imagination."

Hawthorne holds the latest envelope back for a moment.

"Either give your mystery admirer your comm frequency or a restraining order, but stop using my place as a dead drop, yeah?"

You nod, contrite. Hawthorne passes you the letter, watched by a fierce Louis. It reads,

"To the Guardian, my friend and partner in perfectly legal enterprise,

"A job well done as usual! That's what I like to see in a partner. Steadiness. Trustworthiness, even. And a willingness to share the profits. That little AI up there is lonely, don't you think? Best keep an eye on her. We haven't turned up that key yet, but it's got to exist. One access code implies another. That's what I think. And I'm not often wrong!

"All perfectly aboveboard, of course. It would be a kindness, even—I'm sure she could use the distraction.

"With all the usual sickening sentiments, the Spider."

Mysteries linger within Vesper Station, and in Spider's intentions for Vesper Central.
"Feeling ambitious this week, weren't you? Well done, Guardian." —Hawthorne

Hawthorne turns to you with a serious look in her eyes. She passes a datapad to you containing schematics of the Leviathan and transmat beacon details for the Leviathan's Tribute Hall.

"Eris is up to something," Hawthorne says with a tightness in her voice. "She won't say what, and she asked me to relay this to you, personally, ignoring Vanguard protocol."

She continues with a sigh. "I don't like going around Ikora, but whatever this is… it sounds urgent. I don't know Eris well, but I trust her judgment. If we have to break protocol to get something done, so be it. You should go see what this is all about."

Launch the "Duality" dungeon from the Moon in the Director.

Hawthorne nods at your approach. "Guardian. Ever thought about getting an apartment down in the City? Something with a balcony, maybe a mailbox? I found this under my door this morning. Nearly slipped on your mail—and Louis nearly did worse to it."

With an apologetic grimace, you open the letter. It reads:

"To my dearest scallywag,

"I've got a job for you, and it comes with a sob story. I had an agent investigating an orbital station above Europa for salvage. She lost contact. It'd have to be something worse than Salvation vagrants knocking around up there to take her down. All we're getting on the Europa channels now are automated warnings. Old Human ones. I'm not sending anyone else on my payroll after a corpse. It's time for drastic measures—and you, Guardian, are the most drastic measure I can think of.

"The pay's good: whatever you can salvage. A Golden Age station is a treasure hoard for a canny explorer. I'll content myself with your leftovers.

"Give it a look. Just try not to crash this station, too, would you?

"With anticipation, your friend, the Spider."

Hawthorne hurries to hand you a datapad. "This just came in from a communications relay on Titan. The commander asked me to deliver it to you immediately."

The datapad contains coordinates on Titan for the New Pacific Arcology. "The Hive have a foothold there, but the deputy commander says the situation has changed," Hawthorne says with concern.

"Something about a Lucent Hive ship entering Titan's atmosphere and diving into the ocean," Hawthorne says and motions to the datapad. "Details look scarce. But whatever's going on can't be good."

Launch the "Ghosts of the Deep" dungeon from the H.E.L.M. in the Director.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"I'm glad you were able to rescue Bean, he's going to be a great asset to healing the Traveler," Micah says with relief.

"I can't help but be worried about what you found while searching for him. I thought the Psion defectors sided with the Witness…" She falls silent in thought. "But it's looking more and more like that may be a deception."

Micah lowers her voice in suspicion. "There's something else going on here. Something we're going to have to tackle head-on in the future, if we're lucky."

Micah has telemetry on another unpartnered Ghost. "Your next target is Link, a member of a covert team of unpartnered Ghosts called the Watchful Eye."

With worry in her voice she explains, "His last known location was roughly in the area of the Ocean of Storms on the Moon. But he may have moved on by now."

Go to the Moon and pick up Link's trail.

"Some Ghosts have searched for centuries for their Guardian. I know yours did," Micah-10 says with an unseen smile in her voice. 

"The unpartnered Ghost Dejana was last seen in the EDZ investigating Taken activity. Hopefully we can find her quick."

"Come back in one piece, okay?"

"So I found telemetry for Bean." There's a hint of mirth in Micah's tone. "He's a handful, always rushing off into hostile territory. He and I tend to cross paths on remote scouting missions, so the fact that his beacon pinged from Nessus shouldn't surprise me."

For a moment, Micah is quiet. Then, fondly, she says, "But that's what I like about him. No fear, no hesitation. Bean just plows through. We need that kind of energy here."

"Go make sure he didn't get caught in a temporal loop or some other Vex nonsense," Micah says with a laugh. "I'll keep an eye on things here."

"Welcome back, I've got another Ghost telemetry for you." Micah is eager to get to work. "This time, it's Akasha. She's an unpartnered Ghost that has been systematically scanning Awoken territory for years."

Micah brings up a map of the Dreaming City on the display. "I got a lock on her beacon in the Dreaming City, probably still trying to find her Guardian. I need you to head out and find Akasha and bring her back safe and sound."

"I look forward to your return."

"Mars." Micah says it like a curse. "Of course Citrine would be on Mars."

There's a mixture of wryness and frustration in Micah's voice. "She's been obsessed with Warmind hardware for a long time. I don't know how many times Ana had to tell her she wasn't going to build her a combat frame to ride in. Just so she could 'have arms to beat a Hive with.'"

All humor aside, Micah gets down to business. "Citrine means well, but we need her here. Be careful out there, Guardian. "

"I have Ghost telemetry for you, but a word of warning on this one." Micah sighs. "Anwar is a Ghost who has been through a lot. He was once a close confidant of the Speaker. After the Speaker died, Anwar started to question his connection to the Light, and began to seek the truth about Darkness."

"Anwar believes the Darkness is an intrinsic, universal force that must be tended to like a garden, lest it grow unruly. Do not let Anwar's beliefs cast a shadow of doubt on his allegiances. He is an unwavering ally, but one who questions everything."

"His telemetry data leads me to believe he may be inside the Pyramid on Europa," Micah says with a wary tone. "I don't know what you'll find there. Be safe, Guardian."

"I found the general location of Heilung. She's another member of the Watchful Eye," Micah explains, short and to the point.

"Turns out, Heilung was sent on a long-term recon operation inside Savathûn's throne world," she admits with some surprise. "But that was over a year ago. There's been no contact with Heilung since, and I don't know what to expect. The Hidden provided me with her last known coordinates.
We'll have to start there and see what we can find."

"Guardian, I have telemetric data for the Ghost Balthazar." Micah is eager to get to work. "He's an old friend of Peach, the first Ghost you recruited."

With seriousness, she adds, "Balthazar is a scholar like Anwar, but usually not as daring in field work. Which makes my discovery of his telemetric data on the moon all the more concerning."

"If Balthazar has gone to the moon he must have good reason, but we need him here. We need every ghost we can find." Micah says with urgency. There is little time left.

"Please, bring him back, and make sure he's safe."

"I've been observing the energy coming from the Traveler, and… it's not good." Micah can't hide her worry. 

"While we've been doing everything we can to heal the Traveler, the Witness's push to complete the final shape hasn't slowed."

"I'm sending you to find Hecate, a scholar in Hive lore who once studied under Toland, the Shattered and Eris Morn," Micah explains. "Hecate was investigating a rumor that members of House Dusk were trying to ally with Hive broods in the Cosmodrome. The House of Devils have been gone for a long time, though. There has to be something else going on." 

"Good hunting, Guardian."

"Talk about addressing the source of a problem directly, huh?" Micah says. There's nothing quite like uprooting a weed. "Good job. You and I both know the work's never done… but I think you can take a moment to feel proud."

If the surroundings are any judge, the Traveler is also feeling better. Some things might not be mendable, but it's clear that having ended the Witness entirely has made a huge difference. However the Traveler heals and grows in the future, this one great thorn has been plucked out.

Micah says she's going to be sticking around in the Pale Heart—to learn, to help, to grow for herself. She's come to understand some new things while she's been here and is looking forward to more. She might not be right here all the time, but that's the nature of a Hunter, after all.

"See you around, Guardian," she says. "The Six Coyotes know your name."
The Arbor of Light extends its gratitude to you.

"Peach was lucky to get out of that situation with only a few dents and dings." Micah's relief is tempered by uncertainty. "The world outside of the Pale Heart is transforming… We've got no room for error now. I'll get Peach set up in a cleansing team here in the Pale Heart." 

"I'll contact you when I have telemetry on another Ghost. Stay safe, Guardian."

This quest reward can only be accepted on one character, but armor is unlocked for all three classes when this quest is completed.

Return to Ghost in the Pale Heart to decrypt or focus engrams on another class.

"The final shape spreading to the moon isn't a surprise. But that it's hitting the Hive as hard as anyone else?" Micah sighs. "I guess there really is nowhere safe. No promise or allegiance that can save you."

"But ah, one thing at a time, I guess. I'll let you know when I know more."

"The final shape has reached Earth." Micah is weary. "We're running out of time."

With a sigh, Micah continues. "I knew we might reach this point eventually, but seeing it is something else entirely. But we're not ready to move against the Witness. The Traveler isn't ready. Though… we may not have time. But we only get one shot at defeating the Witness. We have to make it our best."

This quest reward can only be accepted on one character, but armor is unlocked for all three classes when this quest is completed.

"We've got a lot to do before we can strike at the Witness." Micah-10 is eager to add to the combined efforts of the coalition.

"I think it'll be the smaller, more humble kind of reinforcement that wins the day," she adds, recruiting you to track down unpartnered Ghosts that can help treat the wounds of the Traveler.

Your first target is Peach, a wayward Ghost last seen in the Cosmodrome on Earth. Track Peach down and bring her home.

"So this is interesting…" Micah trails off for a moment as she reads your report. "Akasha returned some analytics from her scans of the Dreaming City's Ley Lines, and it's troubling. There's Hive activity surging through the Ascendant Plane. Xivu Arath's brood. And as far as I can tell, she's a no-show here."

A thought crosses Micah's mind. "Which means she's cut her losses from the Witness. But that also means she's planning something else…"

"If we make it out of this alive, I've got a bad feeling there'll be another war waiting for us on the horizon. Nothing we can do about that right now, though," she notes with a hint of resignation. 

"Get back out there. One apocalypse at a time."

This quest reward can be accepted on only one character, but armor is unlocked for all three classes when this quest is completed.

"Citrine is so sweet. She profusely apologized for her delay in arrival… and tried to hide the fact that she was stripping the Warmind bunker for parts," Micah says with a laugh.

"I'm putting her with a patrol of Ghosts to help expunge the Witness's corruption and she's taken right to it. And with any luck, she'll put her analytical mind to expediting the process."


"Good work out there, Guardian. I'll let you know when I find another Ghost."

"I've… never told anyone this, but I knew Cayde. Before he was a Guardian. Before I was a Guardian," Micah confesses in a moment of grief over Anwar's death.

She speaks of their time together on Europa before the Collapse, and how she found out about this past by performing a Guardian taboo: researching her own past.

"Cayde doesn't remember. And… that's okay. What matters is that I'm here. That he's here. That somehow, in the face of all this loss and hopelessness… we found each other. I can hug him, one last time… and remind him that he was missed."

"That he saved me."

This quest reward can only be accepted on one character, but armor is unlocked for all three classes when this quest is completed.

Micah bristles with frustration. "If what Heilung has already told me is correct, Savathûn has aligned her brood against the Witness… but she's hedging her bets. She has some other plan in the works, something she intends to pursue after the Witness is defeated. She thinks its defeat is inevitable. I should be inspired by that vote of confidence, but coming from her? Nah."

"I'll let you know when I have more Ghost telemetry to follow up on, Guardian." Then, with a warmth in her voice she adds, "Great work out there."

"I know Anwar's death weighs heavily on Balthazar," Micah explains. "He will heal, in time, as the Traveler will. Perhaps in their shared healing, Balthazar will find new spiritual connections to the Traveler too."

There is relief in Micah's voice. "Thank you, Guardian. As soon as I've pinned down another Ghost's location, I'll contact you."

This quest reward can only be accepted on one character, but armor is unlocked for all three classes when this quest is completed.

"Hecate is back with us, and not a moment too soon," Micah says, tension evident in her voice. The end is approaching.

"The Vanguard are rallying our forces together for the final push. I've sent Hecate out to aid with healing the Traveler, but… there's not much time left. I can feel the tension escalating to a breaking point. I can feel the universe cracking under the strain." Micah grows silent.

"The final shape is upon us, and I can only pray that we've done enough to fight back against it." For a moment, that feels like the end. But then, with a hint of hope in her voice, Micah offers one final benediction:

"Eyes up, Guardian."

The console has been hastily, but cleverly, rigged for communications. When you approach, it flickers to life.

Micah-10 tells you about her mission to find and save unpartnered Ghosts. They returned to help the Traveler as soon as they could, but the Witness's infection caused chaos. They need help.

The console's interface shows an area of the Pale Heart that Micah has marked. She says she's receiving telemetry from a Ghost in the area, but it must be damaged; the signal is unclear. You'll need to search to find it.

She also says that some of the Ghosts have helped scout safe zones within the Pale Heart. You should be able to use them as LZs to travel more efficiently.

The fissure of Light brightens slightly in response to the Ghost's presence. Motes of Light well up and drift toward the damaged Ghost you carry, like dandelion seeds floating in the wind. Micah's machinery whirrs into high gear, analyzing what it can of the patterns in the Traveler's Light.

However, the damaged Ghost looks far from healed…

The Light from the Traveler surrounds you, and something seems different when you bring the damaged Ghost to the fissure of Light. 

Even this may not be enough. However, this time when you examine the Ghost, you see something more: echoes of a corrupting touch, silhouetted against the Traveler's Light. Perhaps this is the true nature of the injury.

"Guardian," Micah says when the feed opens again. "I can tell already something has changed for the better. I'm processing the readings now. Give me a moment, but early prognosis is very, very hopeful." 

It's taken hard work to get to this point, and there's a note of tangible relief in her voice as she talks. Relief for her charge, and for what it may mean for the future. "Thank you," she says. "Let's keep it up."

"Good work as usual, Guardian," Micah says when you return. "I can already tell you've done as much as you can. At this point, it looks like we'll need to deal with the main act—the Witness—before we can make any more difference. Fixing holes only works for so long when the Witness is busy making new ones by the moment, you know." 

Her tone is somberly hopeful—much relies on the capability to defeat the Witness and drive it from the Traveler, but if that can be accomplished then the future will be bright.
A gift for your efforts.

"Hang on a moment," Micah says. "Oh darling, that's a huge data swap—" 

She takes a moment to sort through the information she's receiving from Differential Calculus, the healed Ghost. The data looks promisingly revelatory on a first analysis: the Traveler is hurt by what the Witness has done to it, and all of the lost Ghosts have been trying to help it, in their way—seeking out dangerous places to get closer to the Traveler. 

The instinct is sound. Revitalizing the connection between Ghost and Traveler helps both, although the scale of the Traveler is much greater than any single Ghost. There's still a long road ahead: if the Traveler even CAN be healed completely.

But there is a duty, held by Micah-10 and the Ghosts she shepherds, to do everything in their power to help. And they'd welcome your continuing assistance. "Keep up the good work," Micah-10 says. She has a bigger picture mission in mind: tackling the Witness's influence directly while she works to track other missing Ghosts.

"Nicely done, Guardian," Micah says. She's seen the effects of your efforts out in the Pale Heart, and she's impressed, optimistic for the future.

There's still more to be done. Micah mentions Ulan-Tan, a historical Warlock with theories about Light and Darkness which were considered dangerous at the time. All Light was part of itself, he had concluded: Ghosts connected to Guardians connected to the Traveler, inextricably tied together. Micah thinks—maybe—that the problem with this damaged Ghost is that they've been disconnected from the Traveler in some way and forced to rely only on their own Light.

She's found some places, deep in the Pale Heart, that she thinks are as close to the Traveler's unfiltered essence as you can possibly get. Maybe there you can join this Ghost's Light with the Traveler's again. And even if that doesn't help, you'll still know more than you did before.

"No harm, no foul," Micah says, though she'd clearly prefer the idea works. The slow process of eliminating what doesn't work isn't ideal for situations like these. "Sending you one of the locations I've dug up now."

"Good news, bad news," Micah says, clearly putting a brave face on things. It's a little of both. It would have been nice to find this lost Ghost in perfect condition, but at least they're alive.

The trouble is that it's difficult to know how to help. Simply exposing this Ghost to the Traveler's Light didn't seem to do anything immediately, but the Pale Heart is full of wonders. The line to Micah crackles as she hums in thought.

"Heal one, heal the other, maybe?" she says eventually. It's hard to miss that the Traveler's as hurt as this Ghost is, even if it's in a different way. The growth in the Arbor suggests you're on the right track, but not enough yet. Micah asks you to make a sweep around the Pale Heart, looking for things out of the ordinary—concentrations of Light that beg to be freed, or especially virulent servants of the Witness attacking vulnerable places.

It's just a hunch. But it's the best you've got, and this Ghost is counting on your help.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Starhorse was pleased with your recent performance," Xûr says. "You were a most satisfactory contestant."

"If you entertain the horse further—if you can set its astral mane flowing with beautiful starlight—it will allow me to give you more gifts claimed from the paraversal jetsam. It is an honor to be able to serve such a magnificent being, is it not?"

The sound of clopping hooves plays through your mind, and you feel as though you are being nuzzled on a molecular, almost mathematical level.

"May the many challenges and rewards of Eternity reveal themselves to you," Xûr says.

headerDisplayProperties.name: To the Daring Go the Spoils

interactions.flavorLineOne: Xûr doesn't have much to call his own, but he'll always have your gift. Until he eats them. If he does eat.

"My hands do not belong to me," says Xûr, almost to himself.

"They are attached to this body, and yet their actions are those of the Nine, or perhaps the impossible horse…"

His hooded visage turns toward you. You can see the vague suggestion of his eyes.

"My hands have made you a key, Guardian. They engraved words upon it, but they did not permit me to see what they were. The message was not for me."

For a moment, Xûr looks at the bizarre splendor around him. "Though I stand amongst treasures, I am but a conduit. They belong to you."

"Tell me, Guardian," he says softly, "is it not wonderful to be loved so deeply?"

Then there is a shift in his countenance, reality shimmers around him, and Xûr falls silent once more.

Xûr bows humbly as you approach.

"I apologize for abducting you earlier," he says, "but I was not given a choice. It was the will of the great Starhorse."

Xûr gestures grandly, and you sense the aspect of a horse teasing at the edges of your mind.

"As you can see, the horse has entrusted me with treasures from across the paraverse—realities different from our own. To gaze upon such impossible objects would rend the minds of most, but you…"

Xûr nods deeply and speaks with hushed reverence: "You have been chosen by the horse."

A neigh echoes through your mind.

"I have been told to reward your triumphs in the Dares of Eternity, and I must obey. Go, compete, and claim these fantastic treasures as your own."

headerDisplayProperties.name: To the Daring Go the Spoils

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"How did you find tonight's Dares of Eternity, contestant? Was my performance of the ancient ritual of 'hosting' to your satisfaction?"

Xûr gazes at the shifting aspect of Starhorse. "It pleases the horse when I speak those sacred words…"

He hesitates. "…though I do not understand all that the horse asks of me. But there is much I do not understand."

He composes himself. "I keep another mystery, Guardian. I know of a key that will lead you to great paraversal riches. The astral steed will allow me to create this key for you if you dedicate yourself to its whims, as I have."

Xûr does not wait for you to respond. "Bring Strange Coins back to the impossible horse. This is the first step… and something tells me we are just getting started."

As you enter his chamber, Xûr greets you with obvious excitement.

"Ah, you have already claimed the access card I plucked from a cleft in the paraversal crush," he says. "It guided me to a weapon part, which I have held for you."

"The omniscient steed believes this treasure would be a fitting reward for your complete mastery of the Dares of Eternity. Do so, and this mechanism shall be yours."

Xûr pauses. "Guardian," he begins, then wrings his hands.

He takes a breath. "These Dares of Eternity are not truly real. They are a paraversal remainder, and when the impossible horse leaves us and the realities realign, they will disappear forever. It will be as though they never existed."

"My memories of hosting, of the time I spent with you… they will disappear along with the Dares." 

"Please, keep the treasures of this place close, so that you are reminded of the time we shared. Remember for me when I cannot."

Xûr's expression does not change, but you feel an aura of deep melancholy emanating from him… yet mixed with that sadness, there is fierce pride.

"Guardian?" Xûr adds.

"Thank you for playing."

"Greetings, Guardian," Xûr says slowly as you arrive in his impossible space. "I have knowledge of a matter that was once lost, but is now prepared to come home."

The expression on his face is serene. "There is comfort in returning matter to its correct place, is there not?"

Before you can answer, he opens his palm. A swirling of particles, fine as iron filings, form a familiar face: Shaw Han. "This legend begins where all new legends do: the Cosmodrome," Xûr says. "Where it ends is up to you."

"The trumpet sounds again, Guardian," he whispers, and that is all.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Guardian!" Shaxx's voice booms through the Tower. "As we ready ourselves for war, we also ready ourselves for the Guardian Games. Do you know why?"

He leans in closer. "Every game contains a lesson. Eva's is simple but necessary. It doesn't matter if the stakes are a trophy or all our lives: victory comes to those who best understand themselves."

"If you're a Titan, be the wall that others break on. Hunters, find your triumph in guile! Warlocks… turn your wisdom into weaponry."

"You are the champions of the City. Fight and win. Now and forever." Shaxx crosses his arms and nods to you. "Now enter the Crucible and show me you understand."

"I see you've found your edge," Shaxx says with a nod.

"That's a good start, but the hard part is keeping it. Diligence and discipline, Guardian. I look forward to seeing your future matches."
Lord Shaxx has a gift for you: a Ghost Shell that will track your victories.
"Wonderful! You look stronger already. I look forward to the heights you will climb!" —Lord Shaxx
As boisterous as ever, Shaxx speaks warmly (and loudly) of Crimson Days—and of his challenge to Guardians who choose to celebrate with him in the Crucible.
It seems unlikely that Shaxx will remove his helmet to consume the cookies, but that doesn't mean he isn't grateful.
"Wonderful! You look stronger already. I look forward to the heights you will climb!" —Lord Shaxx

"Tell me this, Guardian," Lord Shaxx bellows, his horned helmet towering over you. "Did the Cosmodrome sufficiently hone you? Are you prepared to face all the Darkness can muster?"

"You're a fool if you think so. All blades dull with time; keeping yours sharp is a matter of diligence and discipline. For that end, I created the Crucible."

He gestures at an array of screens streaming video footage of Guardians battling each other.

"Pit yourself against your fellow Lightbearers, and we'll see if you have your edge yet."

Shaxx invites you to participate in Crucible matches against other Guardians and to complete the Crucible bounties he offers.

Shaxx brightens as you approach, visibly standing taller as your presence registers.

"There you are, Guardian! I'd hoped to see you today. I've designed a new Crucible experience—for improvement, for friendly competition, and the glory of being hailed throughout the City for your skills!

"That last part will come with time. Everyone starts from the same place, after all. Once you've fought a few matches, I'll pair you with opponents who will sharpen you to a razor's edge.

"Well? Want to give the competition a try?"

Lord Shaxx shifts from foot to foot like a giddy schoolchild. His remaining horn waggles in the breeze.

"Guardian!" he greets you, barely containing his enthusiasm. "I have some thrilling news."

"I'm hereby opening THREE NEW CRUCIBLE ARENAS!" His bellowing attracts several nearby Lightbearers.

"The first is a defunct research facility, reclaimed from the Fallen. It's built right into an ice shelf on Europa!"

More Guardians begin to hover around interestedly.

"The second is on Neptune. I've convinced the Neomuni to donate a mall as a Crucible site!"

The group of intrigued Lightbearers is growing. Shaxx begins gesturing broadly, playing to the audience.

"And finally," he announces. "I have secured the most prestigious battleground of them all… A CAPTURED PYRAMID!"

"And not just any Pyramid," Shaxx continues. "The fell lair of the famous, the notorious, Final God of Pain himself… NEZAREC!"

There's a clamor as the eager crowd closes in.

"See you on the battlefield!" Shaxx shouts to you over the din.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
You can now shape and reshape weapons using the Relic on Mars.

Activating the Relic has awakened Resonant weapons across the system. Extract the Pattern mod or dismantle these Deepsight Resonant weapons to acquire progress toward additional weapon Patterns.

With this new information, return to Ikora in the Enclave on Mars.

Gather Resonant materials like Resonant Alloys, Ascendant Alloys, and Patterns to create and customize your favorite weapons.

Level up the weapons to unlock better components by using the Shaped weapon in combat and activities.

There is no limit to the number of times a weapon can be reshaped. Experimentation with different components is highly encouraged.

Continue to find Resonant weapons and extract the Resonant mod or dismantle the weapon to make progress on Weapon Patterns.

Patterns and various materials are required to customize your weapons during shaping.

As you shape and level weapons, you'll unlock new traits to experiment with. 

Ascendant Alloys will help unlock Enhanced Traits, making your Shaped weapons far more lethal than their normally acquired versions.

Deepsight Resonance extraction can award Patterns.

Patterns unlock the ability to shape a new weapon using various currencies for customization and fine-tuning.

Your Ascendant Alloys have unlocked new capabilities for Shaped weapons. Is this a memory of what was, or what could be?

After Shaped weapons are leveled, Ascendant Alloys can be used to upgrade your traits to become Enhanced Traits with improved functionality. 

To obtain more Ascendant Alloys, participate in weekly campaign missions and The Witch Queen offensive activities.

Deepsight Resonant weapon Pattern extraction can award Pattern progress.

Patterns unlock the ability to shape a new weapon using Resonant materials for customization and fine-tuning.

A Shaped weapon can be continually enhanced by reshaping it with new components and perks.

The higher the level, the higher the quality of components available.

Take the Enigma to the Relic on Mars and reshape it.
The vision of a foundry weapon dances across your mind, its shape half-remembered. It will take effort to fully understand it.
A vision of a foundry weapon dances across your mind, its shape half-remembered. It will take effort to fully understand it and give it shape.
A clawing at the back of your mind: your Deepsight stirs. The memory of a weapon appears in your mind, but you can't yet make it clear.

The shadow of power manifests in your thoughts. An intense wave of certitude grips you. To discover the true power of these weapons, their shapes must ascend.

Ascendant Alloys are a rare material used in weapon crafting that can improve a trait into an Enhanced Trait.

Obtain one by completing a weekly campaign mission.
You have shaped your first weapon: the Enigma. However, further increasing a Shaped weapon's level can unlock additional capabilities.

Activating the Relic has awakened Resonant weapons and activated latent features of others. These weapons can be obtained through world drops and activities and contain Deepsight Resonance. Extraction of the Pattern mod or dismantling of the weapon will make progress toward Weapon Patterns. 

Weapon Patterns are primarily obtained through Deepsight Resonance, and occasionally as a reward from specific quests.
Your mind focuses on a vision of the City's foundries. Their weapons have not yet reached their innate potential.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
You open a letter written formally and stamped with the Cormorant Seal:

Rookie,

A Praxic Guardian's education never stops. You've got more to learn about yourself and your Blade, and so do I. 

If we're going to change the Order, we need to work at it. Come see me upstairs when you've got a moment.

Ever forward,
Aunor

P.S. Try the Ether Fizz House of Kings style sometime. Don't let the price on the receipt scare you off: it's worth every credit.
Collect your Exotic armor reward for completing all missions on Legendary difficulty.
Collect your Powerful Gear reward for completing all missions on Legendary difficulty.

"Years ago, my Ghost lost her voice when I got us into an ice-cold situation on one of the Cabal Emperor's Athenaeum worlds. A couple other Lights didn't make it out, but thanks to her, I did. Hand to my heart, I regret it—and I thought she and I were making progress, especially after Kepler. She's clearly holding some grudges, but—thanks for helping her just the same. Now let's see what we can do to take this fight to the Imperium." —The Drifter

Aunor speaks quietly into her earpiece, then closes the call and waves you over. "We're all set for the job on Venus, Guardian. Drifter's sent word: reality and his visions are converging. It's time."

Aunor sets down her datapad. "We need to be ready for the upcoming battles. And if that means breaking with a fundamental tradition of the Praxic Order… then that's just what I'll do." 

She beckons you forward.

We've established a tenuous business relationship with the Pikers, and Drifter has helped us set up an exchange with them: They'll bring a Splicer Shank to help us extract further data from Imperium installations on the whereabouts, defenses, and operational status of Nightfall.
The Drifter is certain that the Nine are involved with the Barant Imperium, controlling them through Bael. They've shown him a new vision, which he's about to share with you…

Aunor would like our help discovering what the newly emerged Dredgen Bael is up to, alongside the crime syndicates of Mars. 
 
Start by assisting her in targeting syndicate operatives across the system to help discover their long-term plans.

There's an empty glass on the bar behind Aunor. She pushes it away as you approach, but her hands are steady.

"Guardian. As much as I'd love to find that bastard and wring his neck… we can't." She spits the words like a curse. "Not while Nightfall's still in the sky. Taking that weapon down has to be our top priority. So, let's get started."
Defy Vanguard orders and delve into the criminal underworld of Tharsis to confront the rising Barant Imperium… Drifter is certain the Imperium and the Nine are connected.

The barkeep flags you down before you can leave the Cantina and draws your attention to a crumpled receipt tucked under Aunor's envelope. On its back side is a second note from her, this one written in far more haste:

Guardian, 

You showed me I was wrong about the Darkness. Eido showed me I was wrong about the Prophecy. The people of the City deserve to know what we're all up against—so we can face it together.

The Syndicates are scrambling for resources and territory. All eyes are on them, and that means plenty of cover for this unauthorized action.

Eido has a line on a busted broadcaster. Parts for repair have to be available somewhere, but we're coming up empty. Help us fix it. Let's blow this thing wide open. 

Ever forward,
Aunor

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Devrim greets you with a stern, but familiar nod. 

"Got it done just in time, Guardian. The fight's far from over, but with you in it, I'd wager we've got a chance."

"Welcome to Call to Arms, Guardian. Gather the best gear you can and put it to the test. "

"I'll have new shipments of the latest gear every day here at the Tower. If you're on the hunt for something specific, my scouts can help you find that special weapon you're looking for."

Devrim pats you on the back. "Thanks for helping the Last City during the Call to Arms, Guardian. You've helped us fortify our arsenal, and that has not gone unnoticed. Celebrate and collect your rewards!"

Devrim nods your way. "That was the last rally horn and the Call to Arms has quieted. You did good, Guardian." 

"Well, there's plenty to enjoy as Celebration Week marches ahead. Take advantage of attuning your weapons and gathering Daily Shipments for the rest of the week. Who knows, there might be a little bonus for you, too."

He motions behind him. "I'll need to pack the gear and head back to the EDZ soon. Enjoy while it lasts, Guardian!"

Devrim chuckles, "The Call to Arms was answered. You can relax now, Guardian." 

"Please, take the time to celebrate this week. Attune your weapons and gather daily shipments while you can. I hear there's some extra goods around for you, too."

He shrugs, then sighs. "I have to return to the EDZ after packing all this gear. Don't be a stranger in the meantime."

"Didn't I ask Shaw to take care of this? Hmm, Holliday was right: 'delegate' might be his favorite word."

"Been trying to fix up an old family heirloom of Holliday's for a while now, something to remember her by. This'll help me calibrate the tooling. Only…"

Banshee wipes the grease from his forehead.

"Where did I put those charts? I'm going to need some time to crunch these numbers. Come back in a bit."

Banshee is distant, taking far too long to notice your presence.

"Hm? Schematic? Yeah. Calibrate. Throne World."
"Arbalest… can't remember what this was named after. Either way, it's a handy weapon. You know what would help tune it just right? Getting some data from Neomuna. You up for it? "

"Arbalest… can't remember what this was named after. Either way, it's a handy weapon. You know what would help tune it just right? Getting some data from inside the Traveler's Pale Heart. You up for it?"

Banshee stands at a countertop meticulously inspecting an unfinished weapon.

"Oh. Hey. You new here?" he says gruffly.

"Don't think I've seen you around before. Then again, not good with faces."

He trails off, his attention back to some detail of the rifle in his hands. He regards you carefully for a moment.

"Oh, that's right, Commander told me you were coming. Asked me to get you set up. Got it on a note right here. Here. Take this. It's solid."

His eyes look past you for a moment before snapping back.

"Oh. Hey. Wait, we spoke already, right? Right. Stay safe."

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"And there it is. Clovis Bray's arrogance detailed in line graphs and metrics. Unbelievable. In the height of his hubris, he sought to build a weapon capable of bending time itself…

"Even with this calibration data, I'm not sure what the full realization of Clovis's design would be like. A faster-than-light cannon capable of shooting across star systems? I have no intention of ever allowing anyone to find out.

"We have what we need to complete this weapon refit to suit our purposes. As for Clovis's intentions…

"They can die in obscurity with him."

"This might look familiar, I know. But it is, in fact, not one you've seen before."

"During the Golden Age, Clovis performed many experiments. When it came to experimenting with the Vex, it seemed endless."

"Time travel became possible, but only for short bursts of time, and with few options. It needed an anchor. Something already unstuck from time."

"This… was that anchor. And it wasn't the only one of its kind."

"For now, it's yours. And in time, all will be explained."

The Exo Stranger takes the bundle of brittle cookies from you with gratitude.
"Happy Dawning, Guardian," she says, and bows her head in thanks. 

"I think you should know," she begins, then clears her throat with a soft mechanical trill.

"This is something I'll never forget."

The Exo Stranger has returned, just as the Darkness was inviting you in. Instead of warning you to turn back, she says it's time to accept what it offers. The Light is not enough to face Eramis and her dark council. If you want to defeat them, you must embrace the power of Darkness as they have.

She hands you a "Splinter of Darkness." This will allow you to wield Stasis. There are others like it, all in the hands of House Salvation. Yours is weak now, but it will strengthen as your proficiency grows.

Lastly, the Exo Stranger offers you her campsite. As you collect lessons and keepsakes, return here to reflect on your experiences.

But first, you must accept the path before you. Begin by attuning your Splinter in the monolithic Ziggurat on the icy flats ahead.

The Exo Stranger is thrilled. Not only did you accept the power of Stasis, you put it to use by taking down Phylaks and retrieving her Splinter of Darkness.

Continue working with Variks to track down the next member of Eramis's dark council. Once you get a hold of their Splinter, the Exo Stranger can use it to enhance your own, which will in turn strengthen your proficiency with Stasis.

But don't get carried away. You have a ways to go before you can face Eramis. Now that you've accepted Stasis, you must learn to resist the temptations of the Darkness and use it solely for the good of humanity.

With that, she hands you back your Splinter, now infused with Phylaks's, readying you for the next stage of Stasis.

Attune your enhanced Splinter of Darkness at the Ziggurat in Beyond.

The Stranger seems pleased as you hand her the Splinter you retrieved from Praksis. You've made progress in dismantling Eramis's dark council and shown that, so far, you have a good handle on resisting the temptations of the Darkness.

But the journey's not over yet. In order to wield Stasis against the Kell of Darkness, you must achieve perfect control of the power flowing within you. The Exo Stranger has seen what happens to Guardians who lack this discipline, but refuses to explain herself just yet.

She hands you back your Splinter, now enhanced by Praksis's. You're ready for the next stage of Stasis.

Attune your enhanced Splinter of Darkness at the Ziggurat in Beyond.

The Exo Stranger is thrilled. Your progress with Stasis marks a new milestone for her.

In order to understand why, you must know what happened in her original timeline, one in which the Darkness corrupted all but a few Guardians. When this ushered in a second Collapse, the Exo Stranger thought all hope was lost. But looking at you now, she finds hope once again. Hope in a future in which the Darkness within us all can be accepted, controlled, and embraced. A future in which balance and truth can prevail for the good of humanity.

To take one more step towards this future, the Stranger asks you to approach the Ziggurat once more and embrace the Darkness within.

The Exo Stranger stands confidently as you approach.

"My friend, you have no idea how grateful I am for you and all that we have done together. This is only just the beginning."

The Exo Stranger pauses and takes a cathartic moment to herself before continuing.

"I've lived in a loop for so long, to be able to see this as a new beginning is… I don't even know. Something I began to think wasn't achievable. But now with you, Eris, Drifter, and Ana by my side, it's all becoming so clear." The Exo Stranger holds out a hand.

"This should help provide us even more clarity. And you, even more Stasis power. Once you're through attuning to it, return to me. I feel as though I owe you a million more thank yous."

"I knew House Salvation would fight back, but not with such force.

"They fight with the support of Darkness watching over them. There is a dangerous strength they continue to wield, but we are stronger.

"Wreckage will continue to fall, and House Salvation will most assuredly be there anytime it does.

"As will we."

The Exo Stranger uncrosses her arms as you approach, happy to see you again so soon.

"This journal of Clovis's is more of a boon for us than I previously realized. In my original timeline, there was a hard copy, though it was incomplete. You've finally helped me access its digital form, and with it, we've been rewarded."

The Exo Stranger hands you what she found.

"Our first step in enhancing your Darkness abilities begins with this. I'm looking forward to seeing what you make of it."

"I can only begin to imagine what this weapon was being designed for. Even on a small scale, its potential for harm is disastrous. I suppose that's very much like Clovis, isn't it?"

"We can't begin the manufacture of these components until after some rigorous testing. I won't throw caution to the wind… like he would."

The Exo Stranger seems lost in thought when you approach, but your presence quickly snaps her out of it.

"I've sent a message to Ana. I can only hope she receives it well. Assuming she has any desire to speak to me, we will hopefully be seeing her soon."

The Exo Stranger's demeanor shifts—excitement is on the horizon.

"In more hopeful news, decrypting Clovis's journal has yielded another opportunity to enhance your Stasis powers. I can't wait to see what you do with it."

"Exo training protocols, huh?

"It seems we were right to investigate. Engage with them whenever you'd like, but keep their existence safe from House Salvation.

"We must not give them even a single ledge from which to pull themselves up."

The Exo Stranger seems troubled as you approach.

"Perhaps I shouldn't have dropped so much on Ana at once. In my past attempts to befriend her—across other timelines—I always tried to ease her in to these revelations."

She shifts uncomfortably.

"But we no longer have time for ease. I just hope that by creating a different world—one where the Darkness can't get its filthy claws into our heads—that Ana will come around. If she doesn't… then this whole thing may be a wash once again."

The Exo Stranger shakes it off.

"No, it can't be. This time, things truly are different. You're walking proof of that: you and your resilience to the manipulations of Darkness. So let's keep up the good fight by continuing to use Clovis's research for good. Speaking of, here's what I found this time. It's yours to do with as you please."

The time has come for the Exo Stranger to reveal to you her secret.

In another timeline, her original timeline, she failed to stop the Darkness from manipulating Guardians and bringing about a second Collapse. Since then, she has been carried through time, trying again and again to prevent that dark future.

Looking at you now, she finally sees a future in which she might succeed. She thanks you, then reminds you that the fight has only just begun. More Guardians must take this path towards Stasis. She'll be here to guide those that do.

Keep up the fight against House Salvation and all the other enemies of the Traveler. And don't forget: you have an ally in the Exo Stranger. Return here to learn more about her past and any other secrets that may help you on your journey.

"We owe much to those who fought to save Europa from the Morning Star's attempted nuclear collision.

"Some of it lies in wreckage on top of the Crypt, but not all. Much remains in the atmosphere, and falls now to Europa's surface. With the careening wreckage comes value we cannot overlook, as House Salvation has discovered.

"We must continue the fight against them and prevent them from acquiring anything that aids their continued violence.

"Look for the falling debris; there, you will find House Salvation. They must be stopped."

The Exo Stranger is pleased with your progress acquiring and learning to use Stasis, but explains it can still be further enhanced.

She reveals herself to be Elisabeth "Elsie" Bray, granddaughter of Clovis Bray I. His experiments on Europa were filled with deceptions and secrets—the most important of which may have involved Exos, Darkness, and by association, Stasis.

Acquire his digital journal, and you're bound to discover further truths about Stasis. But the journal is currently locked.

The Exo Stranger removes a symbol from her own body and hands it to you, calling it a Skeleton Key. In order to access the journal, you must first empower the Skeleton Key with Stasis energy.

Follow the Exo Stranger's guidance to empower the Skeleton Key.

"Darkness energy radiates from Kell's Rising, and that can only mean one thing: Stasis.

It seems our journey to unlock the remaining secrets of Stasis continues."

The Exo Stranger beckons you closer. "Time and again, Stasis has changed itself. New forms arisen in the formations of crystal; new order given to chaotic molecules." 

She demonstrates for you. A pattern of crystals spin out from her fingertips, latticing into a new and stable construct. 

"Let me teach you this one," she says then. "I think you will find it… enriching."

A new grenade is available for purchase from The Exo Stranger.

The Exo Stranger has poured over Clovis's digital journal and discovered that despite learning more about Stasis from the available pages, much of it is still encrypted. Turns out, Clovis didn't trust many, including his family.

Though this is not the Exo Stranger's first time seeing it, she has never been able to fully decrypt it to further understand its secrets. But with you at her side, decrypting the journal finally feels like a reality.

In order to decrypt and explore it further, the Exo Stranger once again asks you to empower the Skeleton Key with Stasis energy, believing that Clovis installed it in her hoping she would use it to one day continue his work and further his legacy.

Follow the Exo Stranger's guidance to empower the Skeleton Key.

The Stranger sighs with relief upon your approach. "It appears, as usual, that when it comes to the secrets of Clovis, there are always more hidden away.

"The old man was… is, rather, nothing if not insanely overprotective. As such, we cannot access it without a potency of Darkness energy.

"Fortunately for us, there's been a surge of just such an energy within the twisted caverns of the Vex here on Europa.

"Take the Skeleton Key and investigate the surge. If I'm right, it should give us what we need to unlock a further understanding of Stasis."

Decrypting a portion of the journal has yielded more Stasis knowledge. It's only a matter of time before you know all of what Clovis knew.

There is work yet to be done and pages still to decrypt to further understand and acquire all that Clovis knew about Stasis.

In order to further decrypt the journal, you'll need to empower the Skeleton Key with Stasis energy.

Follow the Exo Stranger's guidance to empower the Skeleton Key.

"The BT-7707 was prototyped as a weapon to combat the Vex; a portable mass driver capable of firing rounds that moved beyond relativistic speeds."

"I don't know if it was ever completed in this timeline, but a version of it was pulled from another by Clovis during experiments with Vex technology. But it was never completed."

"The plans exist here, now, and I intend to prevent them from falling into the wrong hands. I'll need your help to do it."⁠

With Clovis's journal fully decrypted, The Exo Stranger has tracked your final Stasis learnings to the Giant Exo Head within Creation inside Bray Exoscience.

It appears that to unlock it, you'll need to empower the Skeleton Key with Stasis one final time, before bringing it to the Giant Exo Head.

Follow the Exo Stranger's guidance to empower the Skeleton Key.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Ikora reckons with the revelation that she may be partly responsible for Savathûn's theft of the Light. But with the news that Savathûn also intends to pull the Traveler into her throne world and seal it away, there is no time to lose. She sends you to Fynch to follow up on another lead.

Complete "The Cunning" mission in the Throne World.

"The Light alone does not make one a Guardian," Ikora says warmly as you approach. "Dedication, bravery, the will to protect those who can't protect themselves… they are what define us. And you are a shining example of them all. Thank you."

You have completed the Legendary campaign. Please select your reward.

Ikora believes that when you picked up Sagira's shell, you heard a fragment of a memory belonging to Savathûn. Your interaction with the Relic unlocked a new ability in you, one related to Darkness. She believes you can strengthen this ability at the Europan Pyramid, and in doing so, gain access to the full memory linked to Sagira's shell.

Complete "The Communion" mission at the Europan Pyramid.
Ikora gives a small smile at the familiar-looking confection. Perhaps her connection to the Traveler runs deeper than you thought.

With Savathûn dead, Ikora wants your help answering some lingering questions about the Witness. Queen Mara Sov has requested your presence, and Ikora believes she has vital information to share.

Meet Mara Sov, Queen of the Awoken, near the Relic.

Ikora is daunted by the news of the Lucent Hive. She wants answers, but first, she asks you to visit the Pyramid Relic. She believes the fragment you found on Savathûn's ship might be a related artifact.

Visit the Relic in the Enclave on Mars, then report back to Ikora.

Ikora is intrigued by your discovery: the Relic is capable of shaping objects based on memories. She believes there is more to learn from this device, but the threat of Savathûn must take precedence. Ikora asks you to search for answers in the Witch Queen's throne world.

Complete "The Investigation" mission in the Throne World.

Ikora believes the secret we learned from the worm familiar is the key to stopping Savathûn's ritual to pull the Traveler into her throne world. This information could be enough to destabilize her. But you'll need to reveal the memory to Savathûn herself…

As you speak, the ritual is already beginning. Complete "The Ritual" mission in the Throne World.

Ikora explains that there's a final step to accessing the memory linked to Sagira's shell. You need to locate a concentration of psychic energy that will help manifest the memory. The Hidden have identified such a location in Savathûn's throne world.

Complete "The Mirror" mission in the Throne World.
